questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Rwanda?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Rwanda article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Rwanda?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Rwanda on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Rwanda article.

questions.proof: Rwanda is bordered by Uganda to the north, Tanzania to the east, Burundi to the south, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Nyabarongo-Kagera eventually drains into Lake _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Lake”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Rivers & lakes” part of the Rwanda article.

questions.proof: The Nyabarongo-Kagera eventually drains into Lake Victoria.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “During the Scramble for Africa, _____ conquered Rwanda.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Africa”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Rwanda article, under the heading “Colonialism”.

questions.proof: During the Scramble for Africa, Belgium conquered Rwanda.

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “bordered”. It names one thing, not an action.
